Subject: Purchase path question — AWS Marketplace vs private offer for Mendel

Hi Irene,

Mendel is a healthcare org, so data residency and an auditable procurement trail are priorities.

High level asks:
- Which path typically shortens procurement timelines for mid-market healthcare customers?
- Any implications for co-sell / reseller credits if we go marketplace vs direct?
- Does a marketplace purchase affect ability to receive a formal PO and have Redwood as seller of record?
- Any known gotchas for Mendel (SAML, billing IDs, SOC2 evidence access)?

We'd like a short note to share internally today if possible. If helpful, cc'ing our procurement inbox.

Subject: Re: Purchase path question — AWS Marketplace vs private offer for Mendel

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list. Quick executive summary below and I attached a concise matrix and onboarding checklist for your procurement team.

Executive summary (short):
- Marketplace (Private Offer via AWS/Azure/GCP): fastest to show on-cloud billing, simplifies reseller/payment flow for some customers, and can be easiest when procurement requires a marketplace invoice record. Private offers keep the benefits of marketplace while allowing negotiated pricing.
- Direct (Signed MSA + PO): better when you need Redwood to be seller-of-record on your invoice, require custom SLAs, or want consolidated enterprise invoicing and SSO integrations pinned to a contract. Often better for customers with strict contractual terms or specific data residency clauses.

Tradeoffs and pragmatic guidance for Mendel (healthcare):
- Timeline: Private offer usually shortens initial procurement (private offer + PO) because it fits marketplace workflows. However, if Mendel needs Redwood to be seller-of-record on a contract for internal accounting, a direct MSA + PO is often required and can add 2–4 weeks.
- Co-sell / credits: Marketplace route can preserve some partner incentives but details vary by cloud (AWS vs Azure vs GCP). I’ve looped in Karthik for the exact co-sell implications and which route preserves our SKUs and credits most cleanly.
- Compliance evidence & SSO: Both routes support SOC 2 evidence and SAML. For private/on-prem enclave needs, direct agreements give us more room for specific language.
- Billing & PO: Private offer can accept a PO number and still flow through marketplace billing; if your accounting system requires Redwood as seller on the invoice, we recommend direct contracting (or a marketplace private offer with seller-of-record election if available).

Attachments included: Redwood_Private_vs_Marketplace_Matrix.pdf (one-pager), Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx

Next steps I suggest:
1) Karthik can confirm co-sell impact and preferred cloud route (AWS private offer vs direct) for Mendel.
2) If you prefer speed and marketplace fits your accounting, we can initiate a private offer and provide PO-friendly paperwork.
3) If you need Redwood on the invoice or custom MSA terms, we can start redlining and provide PO template.

Karthik — any additional notes on co-sell and seller-of-record behavior across clouds?

Best,
Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Purchase path question — AWS Marketplace vs private offer for Mendel

Thanks Irene — adding a few concrete details from the sales/partner side. Short bullets you can share directly with procurement:

Platform and co-sell notes:
- AWS Private Offer (PO): typically the most frictionless for customers who already use AWS billing. It keeps the commerce in-marketplace while allowing negotiated discounts. AWS contracts still record the marketplace offer; Redwood can be a seller-of-record in certain private-offer configurations (we can request this at offer creation).
- Azure Marketplace Private Offers / GCP equivalents: similar mechanics but policies differ — we can map exact steps if you choose a specific cloud.
- Co-sell credits: If Mendel is part of a partner co-sell motion (reseller/partner-led), marketplace purchases can still qualify for co-sell in many programs, but timing and crediting rules vary. For guaranteed co-sell credit (if co-selling through a partner), we often recommend a private offer created with the partner listed to preserve pipeline and crediting.
- Seller-of-record & invoicing: If Mendel requires Redwood's name explicitly on an invoice, direct contracting is the cleanest path. Amazon sometimes allows seller-of-record to be set on private offers, but that requires extra setup and can delay by a few days.

Operational checklist for Mendel (recommended):
1) Decide which cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) you prefer to run the pilot in — we can prepare the exact private-offer flow per cloud.
2) If you want speed: we’ll create a Private Offer on your cloud account, share the offer ID and PO instructions, and you can issue a PO referencing the offer.
3) If you need Redwood as seller-of-record: we’ll propose a short MSA + PO route. We can prefill an MSA addendum that limits negotiation to billing/SOR language only.

DocuSign sample MSA (for quick direct contracting): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-private-offer-msa
HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.redwood.ai/hubspot/deal/RDW-2027-4897

If you want, we can run a 20–30 minute sync today to pick the exact cloud and get the offer request started. Irene — if Mendel signals the private-offer route, I’ll draft the private-offer request and confirm any seller-of-record options with cloud partner ops.

-Karthik
